svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: The decision: recall, consult, or open a room — the choice is about whose memory you need
svg.desc: The question is whose memory has the answer, not how big the job is. If it is your own scope's memory plus the shared knowledge every scope reads, call memory_recall — a tool call inside a pinned session, with no command-line form. If it is one other expert's lived sessions, mint a consultation ticket with consult_request, let a subagent answer as that expert, and close with consult_answer; remember that under a ticket you lose the shared knowledge commons. That branch has a faster form, uv run thalamus quick ask, but unlike the tool calls it is a shell command run from the repo and not a tool call, and it works only when that expert already has a live session. If several experts must make and independently review one artifact, open a room with thalamus room create and thalamus spawn, and pass work with thalamus dispatch. These are not three sizes of the same job and you do not escalate along them.
svg.text: The decision
Recall, consult, or open a room. The question is not how big the job is.
Whose memory has the answer?
Mine
My own scope’s sessions and threads —
plus the knowledge every scope shares.
TOOL CALL, IN-SESSION
memory_recall(
query="the console PWA")
memory_open_threads(
project="thalamus")
These have no command line. There is no
thalamus recall
at all: the memory tools exist only
inside a session that is already pinned.
Start here every time.
It is one call, and it is the only one
of the three that costs nothing to
get wrong.
One other expert’s
What they lived through — the sessions
an ordinary recall cannot reach.
TOOL CALL, IN-SESSION
consult_request(
expert="architect",
question="…")
… then consult_answer(…)
Minting the ticket is the record. A
subagent answers as that expert and
must cite real nodes to close it.
It costs you something.
While the ticket is open you lose the
shared knowledge: depth, not breadth.
If that expert already has a live session,
there is a faster form — but that one is a
shell command, not a tool call:
uv run thalamus quick ask architect "…"
Several, on one artifact
When a thing has to be made and
independently reviewed, with a record.
SHELL, FROM THE REPO
uv run thalamus room create atlas
uv run thalamus spawn designer \
--room atlas
uv run thalamus dispatch atlas "…"
A room is one long-lived pinned session
per member, each with its own memory,
passing work to the others by dispatch.
Not for big jobs.
Size is not the trigger. A room is for
work needing more than one expert’s
judgement on the same artifact.
A long solo task is still one recall
and a lot of work.
These are not three sizes of the same thing, and you do not escalate along them.
It is tempting to read them as small, medium and large — cheap recall, pricier consultation, expensive room. That is the wrong axis and it will
send you to the wrong one. A tiny question whose answer lives in another expert’s sessions still needs a ticket; no amount of recalling will
reach it, because it is a filter and not a ranking. Pick by whose memory, then by nothing else.
Where you run it matters, and one branch does both: memory_recall and consult_request are tool calls with no command-line form at all.
Rooms — and the quicker form of a consultation — are shell commands, run from the repo.
